Atlantic Nickel (“Atlantic Nickel” or the “Company”) and Appian Capital Advisory Limited (“Appian”) announce a record monthly performance at the Company’s Santa Rita nickel sulphide mine (“Santa Rita” or the “Mine”) located in Bahia, Brazil.
Santa Rita delivered a record production of 12,464 tonnes of nickel concentrate in August 2026
Building on a strong H1 2026 with Adjusted EBITDA of US$66.5 million at a first-quartile C1 cost of US$3.10/lb
Results delivered as early works for the underground development commenced, with over 600 meters of tunnels now excavated
In August, Santa Rita produced a record 12,464 tonnes of nickel concentrate and achieved a record metallurgical recovery rate of 86.72%, the highest levels since operations restarted under Appian’s ownership in 2019.
August’s record performance builds on a strong H1, when Atlantic Nickel generated Adjusted EBITDA of US$66.5 million and gross revenue of US$163.3 million. Operations processed 3.39 million tonnes of ore, yielding concentrate grades of 12.5%–13.4% nickel with significant copper, PGMs, cobalt and other by-products. The mine achieved an average C1 cost of US$3.10/lb over the six months, maintaining the company’s position as a consistent first-quartile producer. During the period, the company shipped 49,717 tonnes of nickel concentrate to customers in Canada, Finland and China.
Atlantic Nickel is also advancing the transition of Santa Rita from open-pit to underground extraction. The underground transition is expected to extend the mine’s operating life beyond 30 years, with annual production of approximately 30,000 tonnes of nickel equivalent and a competitive cost structure.
Following the completion of the Pre-Feasibility Study in 2024, Appian is now advancing the Definitive Feasibility Study. The initial works for the underground transition are being carried out simultaneously. The inaugural blast for the South Portal was completed in March 2026, and over 600 meters of tunnels have since been excavated.
Santa Rita continues to operate to the highest safety standards across its operations, with a Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate (“LTIFR”) of 0.63 over the last 12 months. Santa Rita delivered over 4,079 Visible Felt Leadership (“VFL”) instances and 54,300 man-hours of safety, health and environmental training in H1 2026, contributing to a best-in-class safety culture and awareness on site.
Milson Mundim, Country Manager of Appian Brazil, commented: “These results reflect the strength of our operating model and our disciplined approach to value creation. As we advance the transition of Santa Rita to underground operations, we remain committed to continuous improvement across the mine’s operations and processes. This approach has enabled us to increase productivity, enhance nickel recovery and strengthen the operation’s results, while continuing to uphold the highest standards of safety and environmental stewardship.”
For further information:
About Atlantic Nickel
The Santa Rita nickel mine is an operating open-pit nickel sulphide (“NiS”) mine, located in the north-eastern Brazilian state of Bahia. Appian acquired the mine in 2018, optimized the pit design, refurbished the processing facilities, and successfully restarted operations in 2019. Current operations involve open-pit mining and a concentrator with a capacity of approximately 6.5 million tonnes per year, producing a nickel sulphide concentrate. The concentrate also contains by-products including copper, cobalt, platinum, palladium, and gold. In 2024, Santa Rita processed 6.6 million tonnes (Mt) of open-pit ore, producing 31.8 million pounds of nickel, 10.1 million pounds of copper, and 0.6 million pounds of cobalt in concentrates.
Appian is advancing the development of a large, higher-grade underground resource, extending the initial 8-year open-pit life of mine to over 30 years. In 2024, Atlantic Nickel delivered its Pre-Feasibility Study (“PFS”) for the mine’sunderground expansion. The PFS further reinforced Appian’s confidence in the project, outlining a long-life mine with higher annual production, low capital intensity, and a competitive cost structure. Atlantic Nickel is advancing this scenario through the ongoing Definitive Feasibility Study, with early works progressing on underground development.

A fictitious warehouse pickup involving approximately $500,000 in SIG Sauer products led to two arrests in Southern California. The shipment contained firearm parts and accessories from SIG Sauer, a major manufacturer supplying civilian, law enforcement and military markets. Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department detectives recovered the entire shipment. Authorities returned all the stolen merchandise to its owner.
The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department announced the arrests and cargo recovery on October 27, 2026. Investigators first received information about the theft on October 12. The incident involved a warehouse near the 4200 block of West 190th Street in Torrance, California. Detectives assigned to the department’s Cargo Criminal Apprehension Team (CCATS) investigated the case. The specialized unit operates within the sheriff’s Major Crimes Bureau.
Torrance sits within one of the nation’s most active cargo theft regions. According to an Overhaul report examining cargo theft trends across Southern California , the surrounding 200-mile area accounted for 37% of reported U.S. incidents. Nearly 70% of regional thefts occurred within 50 miles of the city. Deceptive pickups represented 28% of cases in the region.
Authorities arrested Arman Mnatsakanyan, 26, and Ashot Yesayan, 23, both Glendale, California residents, on October 12. Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department booking records confirm both arrests occurred that afternoon. Deputies booked the men on suspicion of grand theft cargo. Investigators plan to present the case to the Los Angeles County District Attorney’s Office for filing consideration. Both men are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.
Black-wrapped pallets labeled “SIG” inside a warehouse. Los Angeles County detectives recovered approximately $500,000 in stolen SIG Sauer firearm parts and accessories following a fictitious pickup in Torrance, California. (Photo: Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department)
Inside the cargo theft investigation
Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department Detective Division Chief Jose G. Mendoza highlighted the recovery in a statement, noting that “hundreds of thousands of dollars of stolen gun parts were taken off the streets.” The Cargo Criminal Apprehension Team works alongside other specialized units targeting organized theft. LASD established its Organized Retail Crimes Task Force in September 2023. That operation includes cargo investigators and the Burglary and Robbery Task Force. Personnel collaborate with local law enforcement agencies, regional task forces and federal partners.
Questions remain about the fictitious pickup
LASD has not explained how the fictitious pickup occurred or identified the transportation provider. The department’s announcement also omitted details about shipping documents, equipment and the recovery location. Investigators have not disclosed how they tracked the stolen merchandise. FreightWaves contacted the Sheriff’s Department and SIG Sauer for additional information, but neither had responded by publication time.
Other California investigations have involved fraudulent pickups of commercial shipments. In one case, Montclair police investigated approximately $70,000 in stolen beer shipments involving fraudulent pickup documents . The incidents occurred at an Anheuser-Busch distribution center. Detectives identified discrepancies involving the trucking company, driver and vehicles.
A separate Southern California investigation exposed another method criminals used to obtain commercial freight. A Los Angeles jury convicted two defendants in a $2 million nationwide cargo theft scheme involving purchased trucking companies . The operation involved established motor carriers used to secure legitimate shipments. Prosecutors connected the defendants to cargo thefts across multiple states.
Why it matters
Fictitious pickups present a serious threat when warehouses release valuable freight without confirming the authorized transportation provider. This case highlights the importance of verifying pickup credentials before transferring custody of a shipment.
CFCO
Strategic theft often exploits the brief window before a shipment leaves the dock. Once freight changes hands, the opportunity to control who takes possession disappears. The Certified Fraud Compliance Officer (CFCO) program trains professionals to make that window count through independent carrier, driver and pickup verification. Confidence comes from verification, not assumptions.

Ford pulled the plug on the Escape last year after a 25-year run, but the crossover SUV is set to return as an EV based on the new UEV platform.
When is Ford launching the Escape EV?
While Ford is preparing to launch the Fathom, its first vehicle based on the Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform in 2027, the company is already hinting at what’s expected to be its second UEV-based model.
The last gas-powered Escape models rolled off the production line at Ford’s Louisville Assembly Plant as it retooled the facility to prepare for the new Fathom electric pickup.
Typically, when Ford retires a model, its landing page says something like “we’re discontinuing” it, or “it’s the end of the road,” such as with the Edge SUV.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Meanwhile, the Escape landing page says the “SUV may be taking a breather for now,” declaring the “Ford Escape is tapping the brakes,” with no mention of it being discontinued. Instead, the site directs you to check out Ford’s other vehicles while it’s on hiatus.
(Source: Ford.com)
According to Ford Authority , the Escape will return as an all-electric crossover SUV based on the UEV platform.
The Ford Escape EV is expected to remain close in size to the outgoing gas model, which measures 180.1″ long, 74.1″ wide (without mirrors), and 66.1″ tall, with a 106.7″ wheelbase. That’s about the size of other compact SUVs like the Toyota RAV4 and Hyundai Tucson.
Covered Ford Fathom prototype at the Louisville Assembly Plant (Source: Ford)
The electric Escape is expected to go into production at Ford’s Louisville Assembly Plant in 2029, possibly making it the second vehicle based on its UEV platform, following the Fathom pickup.
CEO Jim Farley confirmed on Ford’s Q3 earnings call on Wednesday that the Fathom launch “remains on track for the fourth quarter of next year.”
The Fathom is “a breakthrough product,” Farley said, adding the pickup is highly capable, innovative, and affordable.
Ford Fathom EV pickup prototype (Source: Jim Farley)
Ford will open preorders for the Fathom in early 2027, starting at $28,350 for the standard-range version. With the $1,595 delivery fee, Ford’s electric pickup will still start under $30,000, which the company says will be “right in the heart of the market.”
The Fathom will be the first vehicle to integrate Apple Maps into its navigation system. It will also be BlueCruise-capable for hands-free driving. Other standard features include Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, plus bidirectional charging capabilities.
CEO Jim Farley presents the Ford Universal EV Platform in Kentucky (Source: Ford)
Ford claims the electric pickup will offer more interior space than a Toyota RAV4, not including the added bed and frunk (front trunk).
Inside, the Fathom has a “large touchscreen display” with an easy-to-use navigation system using Apple Maps.
Ford has yet to reveal battery specs or range, but the UEV platform uses lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries to reduce costs. We also know the Fathom will have an NACS charge port after a few prototypes were spotted charging at a Tesla Supercharger a few months ago.
The UEV platform is flexible enough to underpin vehicles ranging from compact crossovers to pickup trucks and vans, so an electric Escape would make sense.
With the Fathom set to launch next year, we should learn more about the upcoming Ford Escape EV soon. Check back for updates.

Posted By: FREDERIC TOMESCO October 29, 2026
Eldorado Gold (TSX: ELD; NYSE: EGO) shares sank after the company slashed its annual production outlook and raised spending estimates as the Skouries copper-gold operation in Greece takes longer than expected to ramp up.
Vancouver-based Eldorado cut its 2026 gold forecast by 18% at the midpoint, to 425,000-475,000 oz. from 495,000-600,000 oz. previously. The miner also disclosed $160 million (C$224.6 million) in additional Skouries costs, plus $80 million of previously planned spending now expected before commercial production, according to quarterly results issued late on Wednesday.
While Skouries remains on track for commercial production by Dec. 31, “another capital increase and materially lower 2026 production reinforce execution concerns heading into 2027,” Jefferies mining analyst Fahad Tariq wrote Wednesday.
Eldorado dropped 6.1% to C$45.29 Thursday morning in Toronto, valuing the company at about C$11.9 billion ($8.5 billion). The stock has traded between C$34.25 and C$69.46 in the past year.
Execution concerns
The setbacks delay Eldorado’s transition from heavy construction spending to stronger cash generation from Skouries and Saskatchewan’s McIlvenna Bay.
As 2026 marks its fourth year of negative guidance revisions in the past five, “investors will question the company’s execution record,” Tariq said. He nevertheless maintained his buy rating on the stock.
Skouries’ expected gold output this year shrank to 10,000-35,000 oz. from 60,000-100,000 oz., a 72% reduction at the midpoint. Eldorado still expects commercial production late in the fourth quarter and says the slower start doesn’t change its expectations for the operation’s longer-term capacity.
Longer commissioning
Total project capital is now estimated at $1.43 billion, up $110 million, while accelerated operational capital rises $130 million to $390 million. Longer commissioning, additional contractor and owner costs and extended use of temporary generators contributed to the increase. Another $30 million could be incurred, depending on when commercial production begins.
National Bank Financial analyst Don DeMarco distinguished the additional costs from the reclassification of spending previously expected after commercial production. His calculation puts the underlying Skouries increase at $160 million, or 10%.
At Skouries, two of six tailings filter presses are operating; the other four are expected online in November. Temporary generators contributed to costs but have since been removed following the grid connection, the company said.
Existing mines
Weakness also extends to existing operations. Eldorado cut their gold forecast to 410,000-430,000 oz. from 430,000-490,000 oz., reflecting shortfalls at Kisladag in Turkey and Olympias in Greece. Stronger performance at Quebec’s Lamaque complex provided a partial offset.
At Kisladag, slower mining delayed access to higher-grade ore. The mine’s roughly 300-day leaching cycle means improved grades being stacked now won’t fully translate into production until late this year and into 2027. Olympias’ expansion schedule is reducing expected fourth-quarter throughput.
All-in sustaining cost guidance for existing operations climbed 16% at the midpoint to $1,975–$2,125 per oz., reflecting lower output, higher sustaining spending and price-linked royalties.
Cash burn
“Higher cost guidance largely reflects lower expected production, higher sustaining capex and increased price-linked royalties, rather than a deterioration in the underlying cost structure,” DeMarco wrote Thursday.
McIlvenna Bay, in Saskatchewan, is also expected to cost more. Capital expenditures are now estimated at $975 million, a 2.4% increase. It excludes earlier spending before June 2024. Commercial production is expected late in the fourth quarter.
Adjusted net earnings of 49¢ a share missed the 54¢ consensus estimate in the third quarter. The free cash flow deficit widened to $191.1 million from $87.4 million a year earlier as spending continued at Skouries and McIlvenna Bay. Excluding those two operations, free cash flow was positive at $98.3 million, the company said.
“Overall, despite an operationally weaker quarter, we believe that the guidance revision is necessary, as it provides Eldorado with a much more achievable target as it approaches the inflection point for a significant step-up in production in the near future,” CIBC mining analyst Cosmos Chiu wrote in a note.

This Explorer Superyacht Is Equipped for Any Adventure, Packs a Submarine, Seaplane, and Helipad
9 photos
Photo: Burgess/ Delta Marine
Incorporating an extensive suite of equipment for aerial and sea exploration as well as remote-shore operations in a yacht designed to stay under the 500GT threshold is not an easy feat, but Delta Marine has accomplished this with its newest Project Zembra, an expedition superyacht that was launched in August this year and is now offered for sale. And it did so without abandoning the comforts expected of a private superyacht.
Dubbed the American shipyard’s most technically ambitious project to date, Zembra is a one-off 152-foot (46-meter) full-displacement motor yacht that combines long-range cruising with an extensive suite of exploration equipment. It’s engineered to accommodate a helicopter, a submersible, amphibious aircraft, a large tender, and other toys that facilitate exploration above and below the water.
Zembra features naval architecture and exterior design by Delta Design Group, while the interiors were created by The Roger Thomas Collection in collaboration with Woogmaster Studio and Delta Design Group. It was conceived as an adventure-forward yacht, and besides a bold, robust profile , what makes it recognizable from a distance is its full metallic Arizona bronze paint on the outside. Clean angular lines and large expanses of glazing also contribute to its distinctive appearance.
Built from composite materials, the superyacht is based on a proven, full-displacement Delta Marine hull. “Zembra springs from Delta’s proven full-displacement hull platform in the 150-to 164-foot range,” reiterates Delta Vice President Michelle Jones. “This fully trans-oceanic hull design is both versatile and exceptionally capable, continuing our legacy of building true global travelers for active clients.”
Photo: Burgess/ Delta Marine Its exceptional inventory of exploration equipment includes a Williams DieselJet 625 tender, kayaks, Jet Skis, a Remote Operated Vehicle (ROV), paddleboards, and a modular inflatable dock system. For those interested in watching marine life, an elevated bow observation platform and an inflatable FunAir crow’s nest provide great vantage points.
For more daring, specialized expeditions, the superyacht has dedicated storage for a Icon A5 light-sport aircraft designed to land on water and a three-person U-Boat Worx submersible. Four cranes are included to support the handling of the extensive onboard equipment, while a scientific wet lab helps with underwater research. According to the shipbuilder, the major challenge was to make the vessel capable of supporting the additional weight of all the toys carried on the open decks.
A custom 55-foot JR Marine catamaran shadow vessel will accompany the yacht, designed to launch and recover the four-tonne submarine. Both Zembra and the catamaran also feature helicopter landing pads, and the support catamaran has its own integrated A-frame, a hydraulic beaching bow ramp, commercial dive compressors and personal watercraft storage.
Photo: Burgess/ Delta Marine Besides its impressive expedition capabilities, Zembra can still function as a luxurious recreational watercraft, featuring dedicated areas for relaxation, socialization, and entertainment. An array of sumptuous living areas are strategically laid out to ensure ease of movement and daily comfort, while the finishes are carefully picked to make the interior feel warm and inviting.
A five-stateroom layout offers accommodation for up to 12 guests, while the owner will benefit from a full-beam master suite on the main deck with panoramic floor-to ceiling windows. The en-suite guest cabins are located on the lower deck, and a fitness center can be converted into a sixth cabin if additional accommodation is needed. The yacht also includes a gym for wellness activities on board, and an elevator serves all four decks.
As for the convivial areas, the main salon serves as a gathering space with multiple sofas and a dining table. It opens onto an open-air lounge on the aft deck through glass doors, creating a nice indoor-outdoor entertaining space.
The bridge deck is dedicated to al-fresco dining, while also providing a sky lounge, and the expansive sundeck is for sunbathing and enjoying the views, with a forward jacuzzi, several seating areas, and a custom wet bar, plus another al fresco dining area.
Style-wise, the interior is said to be modern and inviting, with custom cerused oak, polished stainless-steel accents, Quintus furnishings, Rocky Mountain Hardware, and Tai Ping silk-and-wool carpets.
Photo: Burgess/ Delta Marine Zembra is powered by twin 1,200-hp Caterpillar C32 engines, which give it a cruising speed of 12 knots and a maximum speed of 15.5 knots. The vessel is equipped with Quantum QC-1800 Zero Speed stabilizers that help maintain comfort, and a pair of 99 kW Kohler generators and dual FCI watermakers support self-sufficient cruising.
All in all, Zembra has many aces up its sleeve, from its advanced composite construction and capability for transoceanic passages to the versatility to switch from private exploration to international charter. What’s more, it boasts Lloyd’s Register and MCA classification, which further reinforce its robust global cruising credentials.
Zembra is on the market for the first time, listed with Wes Sanford of Northrop & Johnson and Kevin Kramer of Burgess. It has an asking price of $69 million (around €61,9 million), not including the amphibious aircraft, submarine, shadow vessel and Boxfish ROV, which are all available for separate purchase.

Eli Lilly’s shares rose 4% in early morning trading after reporting revenue of $24.4 billion, well past consensus estimates.
Eli Lilly’s exponential growth can’t be stopped. The GLP-1 juggernaut once again reported an astounding year-over-year revenue increase of 39% for the third quarter, reaching $24.4 billion on the strength of tirzepatide products Mounjaro and Zepbound.
The results represent a sound beat of consensus, with analysts predicting revenue of $22.6 billion.
Shares of the company rose 4% in early morning trading on Thursday as investors awaited an earnings call with executives at 10 a.m. ET.
Lilly revenue growth chart
BioSpace, Flourish
The massive beat was thanks to a 53% increase in volume, even as lower prices impacted sales. Key products, which included Mounjaro and Zepbound, delivered $17.1 billion in the period. Revenue from Lilly’s immunology, oncology and neuroscience key products grew 100% as compared to the year prior, according to the Thursday earnings report .
U.S. revenue grew 34%, notching $15.1 billion as volume rose 41%. Zepbound and Mounjaro were the prime contributors here, even as the price of Zepbound declined.
But money also flowed in from overseas, with ex-U.S. revenue increasing 47% to $9.3 billion thanks to a 76% increase in volume. This was mainly thanks to Mounjaro, despite the drug being added to China’s National Reimbursement Drug List and its price lowered.
Prescriptions for Lilly’s Foundayo took off in the third quarter, with the oral weight loss drug reaching more than 45,000 patients by the end of the period. As of the end of September, Lilly had snagged 40% of new patients starting an oral GLP-1 therapy, according to a corporate presentation published Thursday. The Indianapolis pharma attributed the success to broad commercial formulary and Medicare access, growing brand awareness and new launches globally. The product became available in the United Arab Emirates, Mexico, Saudi Arabia and the U.K., and is under regulatory review in more than 40 other countries.
Lilly’s incretin analogs now command 63% of the overall market, towering over rival Novo.
Ever confident, Lilly raised its full year guidance from $85-87 billion to a range of $91–92 billion.

BYD’s Q3 2026 earnings are out, and net profit jumped 28% year-over-year to ¥10.02 billion as the Chinese automaker shipped more than half a million vehicles out of the country in just three months.
But the rest of the filing is messier. BYD’s inventory is up 60% since January, its cash pile has shrunk by almost half, and profit is still down for the first nine months of the year.
BYD is still operating at a high level, but its business is changing.
BYD Q3 2026 earnings by the numbers
BYD filed its third-quarter report with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on Thursday. Here are the key figures for July through September:
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Revenue: ¥221.49 billion, up 13.6% year-over-year
Net profit attributable to shareholders: ¥10.02 billion, up 28.1%
Net profit excluding one-time items: ¥8.63 billion, up 25.3%
Earnings per share: ¥1.10, up 29.4%
BYD’s key financial data for Q3 2026, from its third quarterly report filed with HKEX on Oct. 29, 2026
That’s BYD’s best quarterly profit since the end of 2024, and the first time revenue has grown year-over-year after four straight quarters of declines.
It’s also a big rebound from the start of the year. BYD’s Q1 2026 profit collapsed 55% to ¥4.08 billion, before recovering to ¥8.24 billion in Q2.
Still, it came in under expectations. Brokerages polled by Reuters were looking for ¥11.4 billion to ¥12.95 billion.
And zoom out to the full year so far, and BYD is treading water. Revenue for the first nine months was ¥566.30 billion, up just 0.01%, while net profit fell 4.2% to ¥22.34 billion. That’s on top of 2025, when BYD’s annual profit had already dropped to ¥32.62 billion from ¥40.25 billion in 2024.
Exports are carrying BYD now
The quarterly report doesn’t break out vehicle volumes, but BYD’s monthly sales filings do. The automaker sold 1,323,065 vehicles in Q3, up 18.7% from 1,114,192 a year earlier.
All of that growth, and then some, came from outside China. BYD exported 550,704 vehicles in the quarter, up 137% from 232,806 in Q3 2025. Everything else, which is mostly the Chinese market, fell about 12% to roughly 772,000 units.
Exports now account for 42% of BYD’s sales. In the first half, overseas markets already brought in ¥181.3 billion, or 53% of the company’s revenue.
For perspective, Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles worldwide in Q3 . BYD exported more cars than Tesla sold on the entire planet.
At home, it’s a different story. China’s price war hasn’t let up, and BYD is now fighting it with cars like the new Seagull with 5-minute flash charging, starting under $10,000 . That’s great for buyers. Not so much for margins.
Going global isn’t cheap
BYD doesn’t report gross margin in its quarterly filing, but it can be calculated from the income statement. We get about 18.0% for Q3, slightly better than 17.6% a year ago, but down from roughly 18.9% in Q2.
The bigger hits are further down the income statement.
Finance expenses came in at ¥7.37 billion for the first nine months, compared to a ¥2.94 billion gain in the same period last year. BYD blames exchange losses. That’s a swing of more than ¥10 billion when the company made ¥22.34 billion in profit, which is the price of doing half your business in foreign currencies.
Impairment charges are also climbing. BYD booked ¥2.71 billion in asset impairment losses, up 68%, which it says is mostly inventory write-downs because of “the expanded inventory scale.” Credit losses tripled to ¥944 million, set aside “in line with the increase in trade receivables.”
And then there’s R&D. BYD’s research and development expenses fell 17% to ¥36.28 billion over nine months. A small part of that is accounting, since BYD capitalized more development costs on its balance sheet this year, but it’s still a notable drop for a company that has built its brand on vertical integration and in-house tech.
The balance sheet is where it gets uncomfortable
Here’s how a few key line items moved between Dec. 31, 2025 and Sept. 30, 2026:
Inventories: ¥221.58 billion, up 60% from ¥138.42 billion
Trade receivables: ¥56.47 billion, up 53% from ¥37.00 billion
Bills payable: ¥78.86 billion, up 251% from ¥22.46 billion
Cash plus trading securities: ¥71.72 billion, down 45% from ¥129.96 billion
BYD attributes both the inventory and receivables jumps “mainly” to the growth of its overseas auto business. That makes sense. Cars on ships, in ports and at foreign dealers sit on the books a lot longer than a car sold to a dealer in China.
The bills payable number stands out too. Those are short-term notes BYD hands suppliers instead of cash, and they more than tripled this year, which BYD explains as “the increase in settlement of bills.”
On the financing side, BYD cut its short-term bank borrowings roughly in half to ¥18.67 billion, but tripled its bonds outstanding to ¥14.99 billion and issued super short-term commercial paper.
To be fair, there are healthy signals in there as well. Operating cash flow for the first nine months was ¥54.47 billion, up 33%. Customer prepayments (contract liabilities) rose 81% to ¥92.95 billion, which points to strong orders. And cash spent on new factories and equipment fell 24% to ¥87.38 billion as BYD’s huge buildout slows down.
Electrek’s Take
On the surface, this is a good quarter for BYD. Profit is up 28%, revenue is growing again, and the export strategy is clearly working. BYD exporting more cars in a quarter than Tesla sells worldwide would have sounded absurd just three years ago.
But we don’t think it’s as clean as the headline number suggests.
BYD added over ¥83 billion worth of inventory in nine months while its sales were down 3.9% year-to-date. Receivables are up, supplier IOUs are up, and cash is way down. That’s what it looks like when you push a lot of cars into a long overseas pipeline and wait to get paid for them. It works as long as those cars sell at decent prices. If they don’t, those impairment charges we’re already seeing get a lot bigger.
And the domestic business isn’t getting easier. BYD is selling fewer cars in China than a year ago while it now employs over 1 million people . The cuts to R&D spending are a sign the company is looking for savings somewhere.
These are all signs of BYD’s business changing. It is going to take a while for it to settle, but I think they are currently in a great spot with the switch to their Blade battery 2.0 virtually over, and new capacity coming from Hungary, Thailand, and Brazil.

America Gets a New Fiat Topolino, Plus One Built Like a Yacht
21 photos
Photo: Fiat
It's been only a few months since the Italian carmaker Fiat unloaded on American shores one of the smallest cars available at the moment on the market, the Topolino. The little mouse, as it's affectionately called (because that's what the term means in Italian), has proven so successful that the carmaker has now announced the 2027 variant, with a new body style taking center stage, plus a sort of concept car mimicking the feel of a yacht.
I'll start with the concept, if it can be called that, as it is, for all intents and purposes, the highlight of the announcement. The one-of-a-kind build was put together with Italian yacht maker Sanlorenzo , and it was shown in the metal during the Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show that kicked off this week.
Based on the standard electric vehicle, the unnamed design comes with a special interior taking cues and inspiration from Sanlorenzo’s ways of designing yacht interiors. That translates into natural materials and premium textiles used in abundance on the car's seats, dashboard, and sunroof. Why, even the seat belts are custom, and there is leather and nautical-grade wood spread all around.
Fiat did not say what will happen to the one-off design now that it's out and about, but we do know what the bulk of the Americans will get with their low-speed vehicle that's the craze of the neighborhood.
Until now, there were only two versions to choose from, the standard and Dolce Vita, but now a third model is joining the range: the Open Air featuring a soft-top rollback roof. Other than that, the newcomer is exactly the same as its siblings.
When it comes to the powertrain, that means a battery pack that's good for up to 46 miles (74 km) of range on a single charge, and an electric motor that can push it down the road at maximum speeds of 25 mph (40 kph) - hence the low-speed vehicle designation.
The 2027 Fiat Topolino range also gets treated to a new full-color digital cluster, and gets two new colors for the bodywork: Corallo Orange and Luna Greige. The unique Monsterlino, a sound system designed with sound specialist Monster, will also be offered soon for the range. The system is, technically, a grab-and-go affair that can be magnetically attached to the car when not in use in some other way, elsewhere.
Fiat said that the existing range, which launched earlier this summer, is already sold out at various dealers across the nation, and that's why it made the 2027 model year incarnation available as of right now.
The carmaker is selling the standard version for prices that start at $13,995, not including the destination fee. For that, it also throws in a complimentary home delivery, as long as home isn't more than 50 miles (80 km) from the dealer. A complimentary conversion kit to turn the car into a street-legal affair is also offered for the models already sold – the new ones are already configured this way.

Honda Plots Radical Makeover, All-New Accord SUV Coming in 2029
7 photos
Photo: Honda
One of America's favorite sedans (not so many left, anyway!) is inching closer to a major refresh, which is expected to drop the conventional sedan look and bring a futuristic makeover. The new Accord is expected to hit the market in the second half of 2027 as a 2028 model with a yet-undisclosed price bump.
The Honda Accord has been in the Japanese automaker’s portfolio since May 7, 1976. A month later, it debuted in North America as a 1977 model year . The Accord started out in life as a three-door hatchback before being rolled out also as a sedan.
So it has been on the market for half a century, and it looks like it is not going anywhere. However, after 11 generations, 25 million examples sold worldwide, and 15 million sold in the United States, the model is set to transform.
Scrap what you know about the Honda Accord’s design. Launched back in 2022 as a 2023 model year, the Accord is set to undergo restyling. Its current look will vanish into thin air with the major update. Rather than leaning into the current conservative look, the upcoming Accord will get aggressive and sporty, thus shifting toward a new segment of buyers.
Photo: Honda The redesign is expected to be "modern and futuristic," as people familiar with the matter told Automotive News. The future Accord will reportedly draw heavily from Honda’s wedge-shaped 0 Series lineup, which the automaker almost entirely canceled as a radical effect of the EV market meltdown and low profitability estimates. The future Accord will also steal design cues from the recently unveiled low-slung Hybrid Sedan Prototype.
The Accord will trade its large front grille for a much narrower one, flanked by razor-thin, aggressive LED headlights and restyled lower air intakes. The model is expected to get a wider, lower stance and a sweeping fastback Grand Tourer roofline. In the meantime, a sleek, full-width LED light bar will split the rear end in two. The trunk lid will get an integrated trunk lip spoiler.
Honda is also preparing a major overhaul for the cabin. A driver-focused, premium layout, featuring a wider, floating central infotainment screen, is part of the plan, along with a fully digital instrument cluster. Google built-in with Gemini integration and over-the-air software updates will also be on the menu.
The upcoming Accord is also expected to receive the simulated S+ Shift system, which debuted back in September 2025 with the Prelude and is specifically designed for hybrid vehicles, as it relies solely on the electric motor to simulate gear shifts.
Photo: Theottle | YouTube Speaking of powertrain, the refreshed Accord, still sitting on an updated version of the Honda Global Architecture, is expected to debut an advanced two-motor hybrid system, supposedly pairing either the 1.5-liter inline-four or the 2.0-liter direct-injection Atkinson cycle engine with updated electric drive tech, aiming for over a 10% improvement in fuel economy.
The starting price is anticipated to stay competitive, kicking off around $30,000. Right now, the 2026 Accord starts at $28,395 before options and fees, and is available in six distinct trims. The lineup starts with the base LX and goes all the way to the range-topping Touring Hybrid, which is a $39,495 deal.
Honda’s long-term plans include rolling out an Accord SUV with a lifted, wagon-like body style by mid-2029 to rival the Subaru Outback, as reported by Motor1. That is when the Accord should become an all-hybrid lineup, powered by newly developed four-cylinder engines, set to replace the current 1.5- and 2.0-liter units.
The SUV would go into production at Honda’s Marysville, Ohio, plant, alongside a new generation of the Accord sedan , which will be underpinned by a new architecture. With almost its entire North American EV lineup canceled back in March, Honda is re-routing its resources toward rolling out hybrids.
Honda Accord, one of America’s best-selling sedans As the affordable sedan segment is slowly dying, the Honda Accord is still one of America’s favorites, but it is obviously struggling to keep up with the rivals. Honda sold 150,196 units in 2025 and 145,521 units so far in 2026, which means it is comfortably on track to shatter last year's total.
Photo: Honda By maintaining its current monthly sales average through Q4, the Accord is projected to finish 2026 with roughly 194,000 total deliveries. This pace represents a massive ~29% full-year sales surge, marking the Accord's strongest annual performance in years.
In the meantime, the Toyota Camry holds onto its crown, having sold 260,684 examples from January to September this year. Sphera has announced new artificial intelligence tools for its Supply Chain Risk Management software to help companies link external disruptions to the affected suppliers, products and operations.
What’s Related
The additions include conversational AI, a connection to compatible AI tools, and AI agents that assess risk severity and supplier impact. Sphera says the tools are designed to shorten the time between detecting a threat and deciding how to respond.
The launch follows a survey of 750 chief operating officers across the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, France, and United Arab Emirates. It found that 58% said their most significant disruptions originated at least as much outside their organizations as within them. That figure reached 71% in the UAE.
The research also identified specific response challenges. Identifying exposed suppliers or products was cited by 33% of respondents, followed by choosing the right response (30%) and measuring the business impact (29%).
RELATED: Supply Chain Disruptions Are Quietly Hurting Company Revenue
Bringing risk management
The new conversational AI features let users ask questions about supplier and supply chain risk information in plain language. According to Sphera, the features show which suppliers, products and operations are exposed, reducing the need to manually assemble information from multiple views.
The company also added a Model Context Protocol connection, which lets organizations bring information from their risk management software into compatible AI tools. That gives teams another way to access the information when making decisions.
Within Sphera’s Risk Response & Resolution Center, AI agents evaluate risk severity and supplier impact to help teams identify issues requiring a response. The company says this is intended to reduce the manual work of reviewing and prioritizing alerts.
Confidence gap
The survey found a gap between executives’ confidence and their ability to quickly assess disruptions. While COOs expressed confidence in their understanding of business dependencies, only 5% said they could assess the impact of an external event within minutes.
“The boundary of the enterprise is no longer the boundary of operational risk,” said Paul Marushka, CEO and president of Sphera.
All 750 executives surveyed identified at least one risk management activity they would allow AI to advance automatically , provided appropriate rules and controls were in place.

Trailer Bridge has named Charles Gittens its next chief executive officer, effective Nov. 2, as the carrier continues investing in its ocean transportation operations and Puerto Rico service .
The Jacksonville -based company announced the appointment Oct. 26.
Gittens succeeds Mitch Luciano, who left the company Oct. 1. He had served as CEO since 2015.
Gittens brings more than 30 years of transportation and logistics experience, including leadership roles in Caribbean shipping, commercial strategy and business operations, according to Trailer Bridge. Most recently, he served as president of trade for King Ocean Services, overseeing operations across the Bahamas, Turks and Caicos, and the Eastern Caribbean.
Previously, Gittens was president and chief commercial officer of Seacor Island Lines. Trailer Bridge credited him with increasing revenue by 115% during his tenure while expanding services and improving operational efficiency.
“Charles is a valuable addition to Trailer Bridge, combining extensive industry expertise with proven commercial and operational leadership in the Caribbean trade,” said Eric Fabrikant, chairman of Trailer Bridge’s board, in a statement. “The Board is confident in the trajectory of the business, and his experience, together with the strength of the existing team, positions Trailer Bridge for long-term success.”
Gittens’ appointment comes as Trailer Bridge undertakes upgrades to its fleet and supporting operations. The comapny sold its domestic logistics division in 2025; recent initiatives include more than $9 million in improvements to its roll-on/roll-off barges, including onboard generators designed to expand refrigerated cargo capacity. It has also enhanced fleetwide monitoring technology and entered new long-term partnerships supporting terminal operations and tug services.
“I am excited to join Trailer Bridge and work alongside a team with an excellent reputation for customer service and a commitment to the markets it serves,” Gittens said. “The company has a well-established position in Puerto Rico, and I look forward to building on that foundation and working closely with customers and partners to support the continued growth of the business.”
Founded in 1991 by transportation pioneer Malcom McLean, Trailer Bridge operates roll-on/roll-off and lift-on/lift-off barges serving the Puerto Rico trade. Its cargo includes containers, vehicles, heavy equipment, oversized freight and breakbulk shipments.
Why it matters: Gittens takes over as Trailer Bridge concentrates on its ocean transportation business following an agreement to sell its domestic logistics division in 2025.

Nine men allegedly connected to Mexico’s Sinaloa Cartel have been arrested in Southern California following a yearlong investigation into an organized cargo theft operation that targeted BNSF Railway trains and resulted in millions of dollars in stolen merchandise , authorities said.
The San Bernardino County Sheriff’s Department announced Wednesday that its Rural Crime Task Force arrested the nine suspects Oct. 16 during a search of a residence in San Bernardino.
Investigators said the suspects were part of a coordinated criminal network connected to the Sinaloa Cartel that had been burglarizing BNSF Railway trains over the past 12 months.
The investigation uncovered an operation involving numerous suspects and vehicles used to steal merchandise from rail shipments, according to the Sheriff’s Department.
Authorities have not disclosed the total number of train burglaries connected to the investigation or the precise value of the cargo stolen during the yearlong operation.
On Oct. 16, investigators with the Rural Crime Task Force, assisted by the Sheriff’s Specialized Enforcement Division, executed a search warrant at a residence in the 1200 block of East 35th Street in San Bernardino.
During the search, deputies recovered more than $333,000 in stolen retail merchandise, including JBL speakers, Logitech computer hardware, Victoria’s Secret merchandise, Nike and New Balance shoes, and Husky tools.
Investigators also seized four semiautomatic handguns, a drone allegedly used for surveillance, a large amount of cash, tools used to access train cargo containers and four vehicles connected to recent rail cargo burglaries.
Authorities also reported recovering suspected fentanyl believed to have been possessed for sale.
The Sheriff’s Department identified the suspects as:
Jose Navarrete, 24
Brian Iran Fontes-Carrillo, 27
Mauro Ruiz-Medina, 30
Pastor Pena-Lerma, 43
Alfredo Covarrubias-Navarrete, 24
Jose Alfredo Castillo-Baca, 24
Jose Ismael Palafox-Bernal, 18
Cesar Daniel Navarrete-Martinez, 31
Cristian Erubiel Navarrete-Zapien, 23
All nine suspects were identified as residents of Mexico and were booked into the Central Detention Center in San Bernardino County.
Authorities said the suspects face charges including conspiracy, theft of railroad property and possession of a controlled substance while armed.
The Sheriff’s Department did not specify the alleged role of each suspect in the cargo theft operation or provide details about how investigators established the suspected connections to the Sinaloa Cartel.
The arrests come as freight railroads and other transportation providers confront the threat of organized cargo theft, which can disrupt shipments and generate substantial losses for shippers and retailers.
In this case, investigators said the criminal network used multiple vehicles and coordinated activities to target trains carrying retail merchandise.
Authorities did not disclose whether the targeted trains were moving through San Bernardino County at the time of the burglaries, whether the thefts occurred at rail yards or along active rail corridors, or whether the recovered merchandise represented all of the stolen cargo connected to the investigation.
Why it matters: The investigation highlights how organized criminal networks are targeting rail shipments, exposing freight operators, retailers and supply chains to millions of dollars in losses.

DoorDash has agreed to buy Instacart for about $17 billion, bringing the grocery delivery company and its retail technology business under the same owner as one of the largest restaurant delivery platforms.
What’s Related
The deal values Instacart at $65 per share, a 26% premium to its October 22 closing price, before reports of a possible sale. The deal will pay at least 75% of the purchase price in cash, with DoorDash shares accounting for no more than 25%.
The companies expect to close the acquisition in late 2027 or the first half of 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. They will continue to run separately until then, and DoorDash expects to retain Instacart’s brand, app, and tech products after closing.
The proposed combination would bring together Instacart’s grocery shopping technology and retailer relationships with DoorDash’s delivery and fulfillment services. Instacart works with more than 2,200 retail banners representing nearly 100,000 stores, and DoorDash says its customers could gain access to more than 50,000 additional stores.
RELATED STORIES: DoorDash Expands Into Retail Returns With $7.99 Pickup From Your Door | Online Grocery Takes Record 20.9% of U.S. Grocery Spending
DoorDash expanding its grocery role
DoorDash’s plans go beyond adding more grocery stores to its app. In its third-quarter earnings release, the company said managing grocers' inventory is an important part of improving delivery quality and reducing fulfillment costs.
Its DashMart Fulfillment Services business, launched in September 2025, already lets retailers sell products through DoorDash or their own channels while DoorDash handles inventory, picking, packing and delivery. Orders are filled from DashMart locations, rather than picked from a retailer’s store.
CVS Pharmacy and Party City were among the first retailers to use the service. DoorDash said the model lets merchants sell online without building their own fulfillment infrastructure.
DoorDash reported fulfillment accuracy above 99% for DashMart orders in the third quarter. It also said those orders arrived, on average, more than 10 minutes faster than other grocery orders in U.S. areas with an active DashMart location.
Those are company-reported results for its existing business. DoorDash expects Instacart’s order volume to help spread warehouse and inventory costs across more purchases.
What changes for shoppers
DoorDash said grocers would remain free to work with other delivery platforms after the acquisition. It also plans to let Instacart shoppers keep choosing grocery orders without having to accept DoorDash deliveries.
In a separate message to shoppers, Instacart CEO Chris Rogers said there are no immediate changes to how they accept or deliver orders. The companies see an opportunity to offer more orders closer to shoppers, but that remains an expected benefit of the combination.
DoorDash also plans to give DashPass and Instacart+ members access to both memberships for one fee. It estimates that would save members $100 million annually in combined membership fees.
Instacart continues to grow
The agreement comes as Instacart’s business continues to grow. The company reported 91.4 million third-quarter orders, up 10% from a year earlier, and revenue of about $1.1 billion, up 17%.
Advertising and other revenue increased 23% to $331 million. That business adds another revenue source alongside the fees Instacart earns from transactions.
DoorDash sees a multi-year path to at least $500 million in annual benefits from combining the businesses, after investments. It expects spending to exceed those benefits in the first year after closing, with positive net benefits starting in the second year.
For now, the acquisition remains subject to review. Required approvals include U.S. antitrust clearance, regulatory approvals in Canada and Israel, and a vote by Instacart shareholders.

On its third-quarter earnings investor call Thursday morning, Merck executives touted recent pipeline wins alongside a strong performance for subcutaneous Keytruda and pulmonary arterial hypertension drug Winrevair that drove the pharma’s overall sales expectations to surpass expectations.
Facing patent expiries for its blockbuster cancer therapy Keytruda, Merck will lean into its existing pipeline and portfolio to offset the looming loss of revenue, while also keeping an eye out for potential business development opportunities.
“For 2027, we see it as another year of investment as we invest behind our expansive pipeline and our new product launches to drive long-term growth,” Chief Financial Officer Caroline Litchfield said during an investor call Thursday morning. At the same time, she added, “business development remains an important priority, and we retain financial flexibility within a strong investment-grade credit rating to pursue additional science-driven value-enhancing transactions.”
Merck CEO Robert Davis, for his part, expressed optimism that Merck will weather the impending Keytruda cliff. “As we look across the portfolio, I feel very good about where we are and our ability to navigate the Keytruda LOE,” he said during the same call, highlighting “recent positive clinical readouts” that support the company’s plans.
Leerink Partners agreed with the executives’ assessment, with an eye toward more clinical data yet to come. Merck’s pipeline is “progressing well as we near the Keytruda LoE, in our view, with important Ph3 readouts across oncology, immunology and infectious diseases expected in the next six months,” Leerink Partners wrote in a Thursday morning note.
Another key attraction on Thursday’s call was Merck’s investigational anti-TL1A antibody tulisokibart, for which it reported a Phase 3 win in ulcerative colitis in June and expects to share data details for soon. The company is also expecting Phase 2 results for the asset in rheumatoid arthritis and axial spondyloarthritis. Meanwhile, in the cardiovascular and respiratory space, Merck will present results from a Phase 2b trial in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) at the upcoming American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) conference next month.
For now, with Keytruda still raking it in as the industry’s best-selling drug , Merck reported $18.1 billion in third-quarter revenue, solidly beating analyst expectations. Guggenheim had projected between $17.44 billion and $17.34 billion.

Float Around: This Inflatable Tent Is for Land and Sea and Can Fit Four People Inside Overnight
24 photos
Photo: Sonmez Outdoor
If you’re camping with the buddies near a lake, God forbid you be the last one to wake up in the morning. If you are, you could very well do so while floating in the middle of said lake on your air mattress; we all know that prank. However, one team decided to make some serious bank with a product that embraces the spirit of the prank and really runs with it.
It’s called the Floating Tent and tells you all you really need to know about what the heck it can do and why it's so special. While we’ve shed light upon this design before, a few years back, this thing is so neat and works like a charm that in all the time it's been on the market, it’s gone unchanged.
Photo: YouTube / Atik Family Back when the floating tent first hit the scene, it was considered the first in the world, crafted by a team dubbed Sonmez Outdoor, a brand that saw its beginning in Turkey, and these days, sells these babies worldwide. They do have a US-based website for potential North American buyers, so if you fall in love with this solution by the end of the article, you can easily get your hands on one.
Keep in mind that Sonmez isn’t just some random team that spits out a product that has me thinking twice about spending the night in it, but rather, has been in the business of making tents for years, be they classic options with poles for support or inflatable tents that make setup a breeze.
The Floating Tent belongs to the latter category and does require a pump to be used in order to give it its final shape. Once we do, we have access to a four-person tent that places 43 square feet (4 square meters) of usable floorspace at our disposal.
Photo: YouTube / Atik Family Yet, those 43 square feet aren’t just to be used for a couple of sleeping bags - they can - but it's the ability to do whatever you want with the interior, including laying down a dining table, bringing in a portable power bank, or whatever your plans entail. Some folks are clearly bringing along fishing gear and bait for some very calming overnight fishing.
Think about that for a second: the Floating Tent goes well beyond the average experience that a two-person boat with an outboard motor can offer, in that you can just float out onto the water, fish, cook what you catch if you have the necessary gear, and then, with a full belly, just pass out. Don’t forget to pull down the insect nets because mosquitos out on the water are just something else ; good luck sleeping if you forget.
As for what you’ll be sleeping on - if you don’t wish to bring along a sleeping bag or anything of the like - is a PVC floor, marine-grade PVC, to be precise, and according to the manufacturer, it’s fireproof and antibacterial, not to mention 100% waterproof.
Photo: YouTube / Atik Family The inflatable columns and outer rim of the floor are also PVC, and on top of it all sits a layer of polyester fabric with a 100% waterproof rating. Even if you’re caught out there in a storm, you’ll wake up after it’s passed with everything as dry as, something to do with nuns... you probably know some variation of the proverb. It can handle 80 kph (50 mph) winds.
An acrylic coating is in place too, further protecting the tent, but it’s not clear where that coating is found. Based on my knowledge of how inflatable tents are made, I'd say that this coating is found on the exterior of the PVC, to help strengthen the tubes.
What I found rather wild is that the manufacturer’s website mentions that this one is good for use in all four seasons, which I'd say is a bit of a stretch considering there is no heating system inside, but you could very well grab a heating solution and try your luck.
Who knows, maybe this thing is so impermeable that your own body heat can make the interior toasty. If that’s true, you’ll need to worry about condensation forming and dripping down on your dry goods.
Photo: YouTube / Atik Family In terms of installation, Sonmez mentions that it can take as little as five minutes for this odd-ball glamping solution to be ready to carry you out in the middle of nowhere with your significant other. Bring food and drinks, not to mention a blanket and some mosquito repellant, just in case one makes it inside.
What you need to finally consider is that the Floating Tent weighs 110 lbs (50 kg), so you’ll need some help to move it around and set up, unless you hit the gym regularly, and secondly, this thing has no actual motor anywhere.
So, you’ll either need to give it one very big push, live at the whim of the lake for the next day or night, and then call a buddy to come out with a dinghy to push or tow you back to shore, or just grab two paddles and work your way back when you’re ready; you’ll have to work as a team with your significant other or friends.
Photo: Sonmez Outdoor Then again, there are some low-power trolly motors out there that have been developed for fishing and just work with that. Lightweight electric options exist too, so don’t worry about overloading your floating haven; there’s no mention of how much it can handle.
Keep in mind that since the Floating Tent hit the scene, there have been countless folks that said “yes” and gave it a try, and the general consensus is that this one is a hit, especially since it can be used on both “sea” and land.
But, it isn’t perfect, and as I foretold, there are mentions that condensation can be an issue, not to mention the actual anchoring so that you don’t go off drifting with the motion of the ocean, so to speak.
Photo: YouTube / Atik Family Last but not least, price is a big factor that people complain about. At a selling price of $4,600, it is by no means cheap, and it is because of this factor that some folks have simply said “pass.”. Nonetheless, those that have stepped up to the plate, have actually found it a neat little gimmick to tap into: being able to float around on a lake in a tent.
Personally, I can see so many uses for this thing, including a neat little summer rental service out on a nearby lake. I’ll just take you out to wherever it is you want to float, anchor the tent down, and come back to pick you up in the morning.
How much would you be willing to spend for a night on the lake with the Mr. or Mrs.? I’d be open to drop $50 to $100 on the experience. Would you? Leave your thoughts below because I'm very curious if I need to start a side hustle next summer.

source_document.body:
Quantum computers aren’t powerful enough yet to break the encryption we use today. But researchers expect that to change at some point. And when it does, some of the encryption used by banks, governments, businesses, and pretty much every other organization could be at risk. The problem is that replacing encryption across thousands of systems takes time. In some cases, years.
That’s what the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is trying to help with. On October 27, the agency released a new report, Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards (NIST IR 8547). It identifies which cryptographic algorithms are vulnerable to quantum attacks and provides guidance on how and when organizations should replace them. NIST has already developed new standards designed to withstand these attacks. Getting organizations to actually use them is the next challenge.
Back in August 2024, NIST released its first three post-quantum cryptography standards. As HPCwire reported at the time , these included FIPS 203 (ML-KEM) for key establishment and two digital signature standards, FIPS 204 (ML-DSA) and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA).
Even then, NIST’s Dustin Moody warned HPCwire that the transition wouldn’t be easy. Organizations would need to figure out where their existing cryptography was being used, work with technology vendors, and plan for a lengthy process. NIST followed up with draft guidance in November 2024. The latest report builds on that work, with more specific direction on what needs to be replaced and when.
(Shutterstock/Jack_the_sparow)
The new report doesn’t treat every cryptographic algorithm the same way. Some will eventually have to be phased out, while others may still be used, but at the organization’s own risk. NIST’s Dustin Moody explained that it depends on where and how these algorithms are being used. Replacing encryption in one system might be fairly straightforward. In another, it could be a much bigger job.
The federal government had already set 2035 as a target for moving to post-quantum cryptography. But some systems now have less time. Under Executive Order 14412, federal high-value assets and high-impact systems have until 2030 to transition their key-establishment mechanisms, and until 2031 for digital signatures. These deadlines don’t apply to every business, although companies supplying technology and services to federal agencies could find themselves having to make changes too.
What’s interesting is that nobody knows exactly when quantum computers will become powerful enough to break today’s widely used encryption. It could still be years away. But there’s another problem. Attackers could be collecting encrypted data right now, even if they can’t read it yet. The idea is to hold onto that information until quantum computers become capable of decrypting it. It’s a threat known as “harvest now, decrypt later.”
For some information, that might not matter much. But think about government secrets, medical records, or sensitive business data that needs to stay private for decades. Even if it’s encrypted today, that protection might not hold up forever.
Also, it’s not as though organizations can just install an update and be done with it. Encryption is used in all sorts of places, from everyday applications to older equipment that may have been running for years.
Some systems will be easier to update than others. There are vendors to work with, compatibility issues to sort out, and testing to be done. That’s a lot of work, especially for large organizations that may not even have a complete picture of where their existing cryptography is being used.
(Shutterstock/Corona-Borealis-Studio)
Organizations don’t have to replace everything at once. Moody suggests starting with the most sensitive information, especially data that needs to stay protected for many years. Moving to FIPS 203 for key establishment could be a good place to start. But there’s only so much an organization can do on its own. It also depends on the software and hardware it uses, and whether the companies providing them are ready. NIST says the entire cryptographic supply chain needs to be considered.
The report also discusses something called hybrid cryptography. Basically, it means using conventional cryptographic methods alongside the newer post-quantum ones. That way, organizations aren’t relying entirely on one method. There is a downside, though. Using both can require more computing resources and make things more complicated.
NIST is also working on the practical side through its National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence (NCCoE). The center has a project to help organizations figure out where they’re using vulnerable cryptography, what needs attention first, and how to make it easier to change algorithms in the future. This last part is known as crypto-agility.
NIST released the standards two years ago. It now has a roadmap for moving to them. Whether organizations can make those changes in time is still an open question.

Mutanda, the world’s largest cobalt mine, is responsible for a fifth of global output. ( Image courtesy of Glencore. )
Posted By: Cecilia Jamasmie October 29, 2026
Glencore (LSE: GLEN), one of the world’s largest cobalt producers, reported a 52% drop in output during the first nine months of 2026 as export quotas in the Democratic Republic of Congo prompted it to defer converting more of the battery metal into saleable material.
The Swiss-based miner produced 13,700 tonnes of cobalt from its own operations through September, down from 28,500 tonnes a year earlier, Glencore said in its production update on Thursday. Third-quarter output fell 20% from the preceding quarter to 3,500 tonnes, missing BMO Capital Markets’ forecast by 31%.
Cobalt is increasingly being “retained in solution rather than processed into saleable hydroxide,” with “value expected to be realised as export regulations evolve,” Glencore said.
The strategy illustrates how Congo’s efforts to control cobalt supply are changing mining operations. Glencore is continuing to extract copper from mixed ores while deferring the final processing of some associated cobalt, leaving metal available for potential recovery later.
Cobalt restrictions
Glencore shares fell 1.9% to £5.31 in London on Thursday, valuing the company at about £62.4 billion (C$116.2 billion). The shares have traded between £3.32 and £7.07 over the past year.
Congo, the world’s dominant cobalt producer, suspended cobalt exports in February 2025 after prices slumped to nine-year lows. A quota system replaced the ban in October that year, with annual export limits covering 2026 and 2027.
The restrictions remain in place until at least the end of 2027, and Kamoto Copper Company and Mutanda hold sufficient cobalt stocks to meet near-term export allocations, Glencore said.
Its African Copper division produced 11,600 tonnes of cobalt through September, down 56% year-on-year. Cobalt retained in solution is excluded from reported production.
Holding the metal in solution reduces near-term processing costs, Glencore said. The company did not disclose the volume retained or when it might be converted into saleable material.
Copper operations, meanwhile, delivered stronger results. Production from Glencore’s own operations rose 3% to 598,600 tonnes from 583,500 tonnes a year earlier. Excluding the closure of Mount Isa’s copper mine and the sale of Kidd, output increased 12% on a comparable basis.
Higher mining rates and improved grades at African Copper, together with richer ore at Peru’s Antamina mine, offset weaker production at Antapaccay and Collahuasi.
Glencore aims to produce about 1.6 million tonnes of copper annually by 2035, nearly double this year’s forecast, under its growth plans .
Production outlook
The company maintained its 2026 copper guidance of 810,000–870,000 tonnes, although it expects to finish towards the bottom of that range. Steelmaking coal output is also tracking towards the lower end of its 30 million–32 million-tonne target, while zinc and energy coal are expected near the upper ends of their forecasts.
Quarterly production was slightly below expectations overall, with copper and steelmaking coal missing BMO’s estimates by 3% and 7%, respectively, analyst Alexander Pearce wrote on Thursday. Zinc and thermal coal exceeded his forecasts by 4% and 5%.
The full-year outlook remained broadly consistent with BMO’s forecasts, suggesting the quarterly shortfalls should unwind in the final three months of 2026, Pearce said.
Steelmaking coal production declined 13% to 21.5 million tonnes through September, primarily because of lower plant throughput and yields at Elk Valley Resources in British Columbia. Energy coal output edged up to 73.9 million tonnes from 73.5 million tonnes a year earlier.
Glencore also advanced the restart of its South African ferrochrome smelters, bringing Boshoek back online in September and Wonderkop in October, following the earlier restart of Lion. Attributable ferrochrome production climbed 29% from the second quarter.
The company reiterated its forecast for full-year adjusted earnings before interest and taxes from its marketing business to exceed $5 billion (about C$7 billion).
“We are pleased to report a strong third quarter production performance, where our key assets largely performed in line with expectations and previously communicated guidance,” CEO Gary Nagle said.

By the mid-1970s, crushing federal emissions mandates, bulky impact bumpers, and soaring fuel prices had effectively neutered Detroit's golden muscle car era. While the Big Three retreated into squared-off, opera-windowed personal luxury barges, the scrappy underdogs at American Motors Corporation threw out the styling rulebook. It should have been the brave bullfighter to take the fight to the bully Big Three. It was a flop – mostly because there was nothing left to kill by the time it came around.
From Kenosha, Wisconsin, AMC unleashed a low-slung, tunneled-headlight fastback coupe that looked like it had escaped straight from an aerodynamic wind tunnel onto the street. Internally, Kenosha engineers shared a tongue-in-cheek joke about the hottest version of that sweeping two-door fastback, the Matador X released in 1974.
Since a matador is a bull killer and the letter X stood for eXperimental, company insiders playfully dubbed the brash machine the Killer Experiment. Spotting one today is tougher than finding a unicorn, which makes the Matador Red 1975 AMC Matador X filmed by automotive vlogger and all-around car nut Lou Costabile so remarkably special. And that’s before we get to the history of the car itself.
This rare coupe belongs to Randy Maca, its third owner, who got it in 2010. Randy's romance with the model began in 1980 at age 18, when he had already been dating his future wife, Cheryl, for 3 years. (The domestic detail is crucial to the story, so bear with me). Back then, he wanted an AMX, but another buyer beat him to the keys by mere minutes.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile Needing a ride, Randy paid $1,800 for his second choice: a neighbor's World of Wheels show-stopping Matador X packing a 304-cubic-inch (5.0-liter) V8 bored 0.060 inches (1.5 mm) over. That torque-rich bruiser was stone-cold crazy, serving as his daily driver, street brawler, and reverse-gear dragster while he and Cheryl made lifelong memories. Decades and dozens of cars later, Randy still pined for another Matador, but found only hopelessly rusted-out hulks.
Whenever Cheryl asked which past car he missed most, Randy always chose the Matador over his old 1980 Buick Riviera. For their 25th wedding anniversary in 2010, Cheryl secretly tracked down a rust-free, Arizona-sourced 1975 Matador X in Racine, Wisconsin. Too nervous to drive it home herself, she enlisted Randy's best friend to transport the coupe and park it on the field at Woodsmoke Ranch's annual 4th of July car show.
Walking the showgrounds with a hot dog and a soda, Randy spotted the red fastback, dropped his hot dog in the grass, handed his drink to one of his three sons, and hurried over. Moments later, his youngest boy, 13-year-oldat the time, Ethan, hopped inside, fired the V8, and blipped the throttle. Horrified, Randy repeatedly asked his son to come out – only to be countered by broader and broader smiles from the family (who had conjured around the car waiting for the big reveal).
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile Grinning from behind the wheel, Ethan cheekily told his father that the owner was none other than Randy himself. Only then did the man spot his name on the windshield placard and Cheryl's anniversary card, thanking him for a quarter-century of marriage, resting on the white rear seat. At the time, the Matador was a sluggish trailer queen choked by rusted 1975 emissions plumbing and wearing 1974 side stripes, two inches wider than the authentic 1975 factory graphics.
Pursuing period accuracy, Randy had the flanks repainted to apply the correct stripes, swapped leaky cork gaskets for neoprene seals, and ditched the smog gear for a custom stainless-steel Flowmaster dual exhaust off the stock manifolds. To cure AMC's notorious overheating tendencies (up to 230° F, or 110° C), he installed a custom-made three-core radiator with 1.5-inch (38-mm) tubes and a 4,000-CFM fan that holds a steady 180° F (82° C).
Riding on American Racing Outlaw II wheels (obviously an aftermarket modification), Randy's coupe also sports tilt steering, roll-down rear quarter windows, and pointed taillight lenses sourced from 1969 Harley-Davidson motorcycles as an exclusive package fitted by Chicagoland and Indiana dealers. The tailpipe tips are also not factory-correct, but that’s a matter of taste, and the customer is always right in regards to that.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile Seeing how this car is universally acclaimed wherever it travels - across more than 350 shows, this crowd favorite has earned 67 trophies (and counting) – it’s no wonder people swarm around it when they see it. Randy has yet to deny anyone the pleasure of sitting inside – he even let Lou take the wheel for a short drive – because that’s how lifetime memories are built.
To understand why Randy's coupe draws crowds, one must revisit the AMC Matador's eight-year run across two generations from 1971 through 1978, which yielded 395,172 total vehicles. Replacing the midsize Rebel for 1971 on a 118-inch (2,997-mm) wheelbase, the first generation encompassed four-door sedans, station wagons, and two-door hardtops, tallying 45,786 units in 1971, including 50 Machine Go cars, plus 54,653 in 1972 and 52,933 in 1973.
In the 1974 to 1978 second generation, sedans and wagons gained extended 5-mph (8-kph) bumpers, while design chief Richard Teague and stylist Robert Nixon penned an all-new 114-inch-wheelbase (2,896-mm) fastback coupe. Fielded in NASCAR by Roger Penske with Mark Donohue and Bobby Allison, the Matador won five races. Coupe production totaled 109,572 units, comprising 62,269 in 1974, 22,368 in 1975, 16,104 in 1976, 6,825 in 1977, and 2,006 in 1978.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile Available exclusively in 1974 and 1975, the sporty Matador X added a blackout grille, body side stripes, 14-inch (356-mm) slotted steel wheels, bucket seats, and a three-spoke steering wheel. While show-field lore claims 1,500 built in 1974 and 7,500 in 1975, factory ledgers record 10,074 standalone V8 Matador X coupes in 1974 alongside 31,169 base and 21,026 Brougham coupes, before the X transitioned into a $199 appearance package for 1975.
Across its 8-year lifespan, the Matador utilized 232-cubic-inch (3.8-liter) and 258-cubic-inch (4.2-liter) inline-sixes alongside 304-cubic-inch (5.0-liter) two-barrel, 360-cubic-inch (5.9-liter) two-barrel and four-barrel, and 401-cubic-inch (6.6-liter) four-barrel V8s, paired with 3-speed or 1971 4-speed manuals, Borg-Warner Shift-Command automatics, or Chrysler-built Torque-Command 904, 998, and 727 automatics.
Total 1975 output reached 59,582 units, comprising 29,080 four-door sedans, 8,134 station wagons, and 22,368 two-door coupes, including 1,817 Brougham “Oleg Cassini” and 1,800 “X” packages. No wonder Randy has never seen another like his – in fact, in all his decades of attending car meets, he’s only seen one other Matador X, a 1974 car.
Photo: YouTube/Lou Costabile By powertrain, 1975 Matador production included 10,725 inline-six cars, namely 3,925 coupes and 6,800 sedans, against 48,857 V8 models, including 18,443 coupes, while Torque-Command automatics equipped 58,410 vehicles and 3-speed manuals fitted 1,172. Base prices started at $3,446 for the coupe, $3,452 for the sedan, and $3,845 for the wagon, with V8s adding $99. Net output reached 110 hp (112 PS) and 195 lb-ft (264 Nm) from the base six.
Choosing V8 power in 1975 delivered 150 hp (152 PS) and 245 lb-ft (332 Nm) from the 304-cubic-inch (5.0-liter) two-barrel, 175 hp (177 PS) and 285 lb-ft (386 Nm) from the 360-cubic-inch (5.9-liter) two-barrel, or 195 hp (198 PS) and 295 lb-ft (400 Nm) with the four-barrel Power Package. Period testers clocked the 4,050-pound (1,837-kg) 360-cubic-inch (5.9-liter) Matador X running from 0 to 60 mph (97 kph) in 8.9 seconds.
During that same Road and Track evaluation, the fastback cleared the standing quarter-mile in 16.8 seconds at 82.5 mph (133 kph) and topped out at 116 mph (187 kph), while 401s hit 60 mph (97 kph) in 8.3 seconds.

Eli Lilly’s revenue is growing so fast that analysts are continually being caught off guard on earnings day. It’s a good surprise, with billions of dollars earned over expectations, but a surprise nonetheless, and analysts don’t like surprises.
As analysts try to read the crystal ball and provide investors with as clear a view as possible on potential investment risks, anything that throws off their calculations could be seen as a bad thing. So CEO David Ricks and his executive team were asked on a Thursday morning earnings call why guidance has been so unreliable, consistently underestimating the revenue that Lilly will actually bring in.
“A key for investors, I think, is to determine when the surprise factor runs its course,” Steve Scala, a long-time analyst with TD Cowen, said on the call.

Providing accurate guidance is always the goal for Lilly, Ricks said, but the rapid expansion of the incretin market has simply been too unprecedented to predict.
“We’re in the middle of the largest new category expansion in the history of the pharmaceutical industry, and Lilly’s leading that,” Ricks said. “There’s a number of things that have never actually happened before that we’re trying to project, and we prefer to give a posture that investors can rely on versus one that is more speculative.”
He admitted that Lilly’s guidance has missed on the low side, with actual earnings arriving much above consensus. But Ricks said the alternative—underperforming expectations—is worse. “We’re beating on the up; that’s better than missing on the down.”
Following third quarter earnings, where revenue rose 39% to $24.4 billion, Lilly again raised full-year guidance after the third quarter to a range of $91–92 billion. At the end of 2025, Lilly had expected a range of $80–83 billion for 2026.
